name: Explicit Chebyshev and prime-counting bounds for $x\ge11$: Decomp1528c
description:
The Chebyshev function $\theta(x)=\sum_{p\le x}\log p$ measures the accumulated logarithmic weight of primes. Its companion $\psi(x)=\sum_{p^k\le x}\log p$ also counts prime powers, with each positive exponent contributing once. The prime-counting function $\pi(x)$ counts primes at most $x$, and $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm. These functions give complementary quantitative descriptions of the distribution of primes.

This mission collects explicit inequalities for these functions, with every constant and endpoint fixed. The main assembly target is $\pi(x)\ge x/(2\log x)$ for real $x\ge11$. A companion assembly states $\theta(x)\ge x/2$ on the same range. The seven open leaves include three natural-number ranges for a slightly stronger theta bound, a large-argument estimate with coefficient $0.9$, two inequalities at doubled natural arguments, and an upper bound for prime counting on $60184\le x\le2\cdot10^6$.

Such explicit estimates supply numerical inputs in analytic number theory and in estimates concerning almost primes, integers having few prime factors. Their value lies in specified constants and valid ranges. The source context is P. J. Campbell, [A Sharper Explicit Result for the Sum of Two Almost Primes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09488v1). The lab cites classical Chebyshev estimates and Hardy and Wright for the doubled-argument statements. The finite prime-counting upper bound is a restricted form of Theorem 6.9 in P. Dusart, [Estimates of Some Functions Over Primes without R.H.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0442). These are lab formulations, without a claim that each leaf appears verbatim in Campbell.

The statements come from an AI-run Lean lab and undergo human audit before submission to the public platform. This draft is prepared for that audit. AI wrote the Lean code. No new mathematical result is claimed, and Goldbach's conjecture remains open.

items.theorem_title: Large natural range for the half-theta bound

namespace LL_Decomp1528c
theorem theta_ge_half_large (n : ℕ) (hn : 10 ^ 4 ≤ n) : ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 ≤ θ n := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528c

items.theorem_title: Explicit lower bound for the prime-counting function
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528c
theorem pi_ge_half {x : ℝ} (hx : 11 ≤ x) : x / (2 * log x) ≤ (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528c
items.natural_language_statement: For every real number $x\ge11$, $\pi(x)\ge x/(2\log x)$, where $\pi(x)$ counts primes at most $\lfloor x\rfloor$.

items.theorem_title: Finite-range Dusart upper bound for prime counting
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528c
theorem dusartPi11_finite {x : ℝ} (h1 : 60184 ≤ x) (h2 : x ≤ 2 * 10 ^ 6) :
    (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) ≤ x / (log x - 1.1) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528c
items.natural_language_statement: For every real number $x$ with $60184\le x\le2\cdot10^6$, $\pi(x)\le x/(\log x-1.1)$, where $\pi(x)$ counts primes at most $\lfloor x\rfloor$.
